problem_markdown: A homogeneous system has $p$ equations in $q=2p$ unknowns, with all coefficients in $\{-1,0,1\}$. Prove it has a nonzero integer solution with every coordinate of absolute value at most $q$.
solutions_markdown: Consider every integer vector $v\in[-p,p]^{2p}$. There are $(2p+1)^{2p}=(4p^2+4p+1)^p$ such vectors. Each of the $p$ linear forms takes an integer value between $-2p^2$ and $2p^2$, so there are at most $(4p^2+1)^p$ possible output vectors. The first count is larger. By the pigeonhole principle two distinct inputs $v,w$ have equal outputs. Their difference is a nonzero integer solution, and every coordinate lies in $[-2p,2p]=[-q,q]$.
